newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Mideast said threat to Australian LNG boost.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Mideast said threat to Australian LNG boost.

text.p: Competition from the Middle East posed a major threat to Australia's burgeoning liquefied natural gas (LNG) industry, Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Tuesday.

Since LNG production started in Australia in 1989, exports have grown to about 7.5 million tonnes a year, satisfying about 11 percent of world demand, John Akehurst, managing director of Woodside, said in an industry paper for the Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) outlook conference.
"Our major competitors during this period have been Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei," Akehurst said.
But increasing demand from existing customers, including China, India, Thailand and the Philippines is raising competition, he said.
"New Middle East producers are entering the market, with Oman and Qatar already ahead of Australia in their development plans," Wakehurst said.

Woodside is a partner in and operator of the North West Shelf gas project offshore Western Australia, where preliminary agreements have been reached with Japanese customers for a doubling of annual output to 14.5 million tonnes.

Western Australia and the neighbouring Northern Territory hold gas reserves estimated up to 100 trillion cubic feet, a substantial amount, but small compared to the fields of the Middle East, Akehurst said.

"While this country is fortunate with its large gas reserves, they are dwarfed by those in Middle Eastern countries where there is little local market for the gas and gas has historically been almost as a nuisance rather than an asset," Akehurst said.
